title: Mali Empire (c. 1235-1600)
key_facts: Wealthiest African empire known for Mansa Musa's pilgrimage
Controlled gold fields and trans-Saharan trade routes
Cities of Timbuktu, Gao, Djenné as Islamic learning centers
Mansa Musa's gold distribution caused inflation in Cairo
causes: Succession to Ghana Empire's trade networks
Control of gold mines and agricultural surplus
outcome: Declined after 1500s due to succession disputes
Timbuktu remained center of Islamic scholarship
impacts: Created centers of Islamic scholarship and learning
Influenced African political and cultural development
